state.label: Dormant
state.summary: November 25 closed at $26.97 (−1.86%). No market gate crossed. The delayed November 13 short report remains below its positioning gate; current options and borrow are not verified.

interpretation: Below-gate market activity and below-gate delayed short interest do not show forced buying. The newly read court update does not change the observed supply mechanics.

market.note: Completed November 25 market session. Both historical tables agree on the close and range; use the ChartExchange historical-table volume consistently with the reference window. Yahoo reports 6,623,900 shares. NYSE was closed November 26. This is not direct covering evidence.

shortPressure.note: Two delayed-data providers agree on 41,054,446 shares short as of November 13, published November 24; down 3.16% from October 30. About 8.14% of the prior SEC-reported outstanding share count, below the 20% gate. Providers use different float denominators. Fresh under the 15-day rule, not live and not evidence of covering.

borrowPressure.note: No reliable, freely accessible provider with durable timestamps was available. Missing borrow evidence lowers confidence; it is not treated as normal conditions.

optionsPressure.note: Call-heavy activity and near-price strike concentration are observed. Without a historical options baseline, the system does not label total activity abnormal. Dealer positioning and hedging demand are not directly observed and are not asserted.

catalystPressure.note: Ryan Cohen's October 2 open-market purchase is material corporate-demand evidence, but by this October 6 observation it is outside the Watch's three-day current-catalyst gate.

supplyPressure.note: The $32 warrant exercise window closed at 5:00 p.m. New York time on October 30, so no unexercised warrants remain as prospective supply. The number exercised and resulting issuance are not yet disclosed, including guaranteed-delivery settlement due by November 2. Remaining convertible and authorized-share capacity continues to oppose a tightly constrained-supply thesis.

engines.headline: −1.86% on 0.96× 20-session average volume
engines.interpretation: November 25 finished at $26.97 on 6.65M shares per the historical series. Volume and absolute return were below abnormality thresholds. Thursday was a market holiday.

engines.headline: Ryan Cohen bought another 700,000 shares on October 2
engines.interpretation: The primary-source insider purchase strengthens the corporate-demand thesis, but it is outside the three-day current-catalyst gate at this observation and does not establish short covering.

engines.label: Supply / dilution
engines.headline: The $32 warrant exercise window closed; realized issuance remains undisclosed
engines.interpretation: Expiration removes up to 59.15M unexercised warrants as future contingent supply. Exercises submitted by the deadline and any resulting shares are not yet disclosed, while remaining convertible and authorized-share capacity still opposes a tightly constrained supply thesis.

relationships.label: warrant outlet closed; other supply remains

unchanged: The completed November 25 session was below the market gates; the November 13 delayed short reading is still below the positioning gate.

The November 25 SEC filing describes dismissal of the plaintiff's claims and a $3.5M legal fee; it does not announce a new issuance, share repurchase, or change to the already approved authorized-share count. Convertible capacity and authorized shares remain opposing evidence.
unknown: Fresh representative options and borrow conditions, warrant exercise and issuance counts, and covering or dealer hedging flows are not established.

theses.label: Squeeze thesis
theses.summary: November 13 delayed short interest is 41.05M shares, about 8.14% of the prior outstanding-share count. Completed market activity was below the abnormality gates. Current funding, dealer feedback and direct covering remain unconfirmed.
supports: The $32 warrant exercise window closed, removing up to 59.15M unexercised warrants as future contingent supply
contradictions: November 13 reported short interest fell 3.16% and remains below the 20% outstanding-share gate
Convertible and authorized-share capacity still weaken supply constraint

theses.label: Fundamental / corporate
theses.summary: Historically reported insider purchases and corporate strategy are plausible competing explanations, but do not identify current buyers. The delayed November 13 report remains below the positioning threshold.
supports: Ryan Cohen bought another 700,000 shares on October 2
Large cash, securities, and eBay position
contradictions: Revenue remains lower year over year
Options activity may be amplifying the move

theses.label: Normal-market / no-squeeze
theses.summary: The measured trading activity is compatible with ordinary repricing; no forced-buying mechanism is confirmed.
supports: November 13 reported short interest remains below the 20% outstanding-share gate
contradictions: Legacy market and selected-options evidence showed elevated activity, but those feeds are not current

forward: Sustained abnormal price and volume, not a one-session reaction.
Repeated options observations establishing that call activity is abnormal versus its own recent history.
A current borrow observation showing materially rising cost, falling availability, or high utilization.
Independent evidence that short exposure remains trapped while price pressure persists.
backward: Volume normalizes and price acceleration fades after the catalyst.
Fresh short-interest or borrow evidence shows easing rather than stress.
New share supply expands faster than incremental demand.

falsifiers: Fresh short interest falls materially without evidence of disorderly covering.
Borrow remains readily available at ordinary fees during continued price strength.
The move persists only as a corporate repricing with normal liquidity and no positioning stress.
Conversion, ATM issuance, transaction financing, or disclosed warrant exercises materially expand tradeable supply.
Options activity normalizes and no feedback-demand evidence emerges.
